Ford Otomotiv Sanayi AS Announces Major Investment to Expand Turkish Manufacturing Capacity

ISTANBUL, June 7—Ford Otomotiv Sanayi AS said on Friday it will invest $500 million to expand its automotive manufacturing facilities in Turkey, aiming to boost production capacity and strengthen its position as a key exporter in the region.

The investment will focus on upgrading assembly lines at the company's Kocaeli plants, introducing new automation technologies, and increasing annual production capacity by 20 percent, according to a statement. The expansion is expected to create up to 1,200 new jobs over the next three years.

"Today’s announcement underlines our long-term commitment to the Turkish automotive sector," said General Manager Ahmet Demir. "With this investment, Ford Otomotiv Sanayi AS will be better positioned to meet both domestic demand and export opportunities, especially in the European market."

Turkey’s automotive industry has emerged as one of the country’s main export drivers, with vehicles and components accounting for nearly 13 percent of total exports in 2023, according to the Turkish Automotive Manufacturers Association. Industry experts say the investment comes at a time when demand for commercial vehicles and next-generation models is rising across Europe.

"This move consolidates Turkey’s role as a strategic production hub," said automotive analyst Elif Karadeniz at Bosphorus Market Insights. "The expansion by Ford Otomotiv Sanayi AS is likely to encourage further investments across the sector."

Trade union representatives welcomed the announcement, emphasizing the positive impact on local employment. "We support investments that create secure, quality jobs for our members," said a spokesperson for the Turkish Automotive Workers Union.

Construction on the new facilities is expected to begin later this year, with the first expanded production lines set to open in 2026.
